title: Nawate Street — Matsumoto City Official Tourism Website

facts.fact: Nawate follows a narrow former embankment between the southern castle moat and the Metoba River.
facts.excerpt: the long, narrow embankment—as thin as a rope—

facts.fact: The street developed as an approach to Yohashira Shrine after the shrine was established in1879.
facts.excerpt: Shrine was established in 1879, the street developed as the shrine’s approach.

facts.fact: Frogs are a street symbol; varied small shops and food businesses line the pedestrian area.
facts.excerpt: The symbol of this street is the frog.

facts.fact: The municipal description identifies Nawate as a year-round pedestrian-only zone.
facts.excerpt: it is a pedestrian-only zone 365 days a year

notes: Official page actually fetched and the named passages read; raw response and extracted text retained outside Git. Route choices and priorities are original editorial advice. No personal visit, demand ranking, guaranteed mountain view, price or timetable is claimed. The tourism page’s ecological claim about a named frog species is not used; the guide only identifies frogs as a street symbol.
